intro_cards.title: About these notes
body: 7 units · geology to population · drawn for a phone
This book is not “world geography” — it is **Eritrea**. Outcomes: read the land’s story (rocks), water, climate, plants and animals, soils, how people make a living, and who lives where.

units.title: Population in Eritrea
units.intro:
People are unevenly spread. Highlands (better rain, towns, services) are denser. Hot arid coasts and western plains are thinner, with more mobile pastoral communities.

Eritrea’s society is multi-ethnic (nine recognised groups, including Tigrinya, Tigre, Saho, Afar, Bilen, Hedareb, Kunama, Nara, Rashaida). Distribution follows language, livelihood and ecology more than a single “average Eritrean” map.

cards.title: 7.1 Background
body: Prepare map of Eritrea and mark the distribution of the nine ethnic groups.
The nine ethnic groups in Eritrea derive their roots from Nilote, Hamite and Semite families.
The Pigmoid people were said to be the earliest inhabitants of Eritrea.
The Nara and the Kunama ethnic groups are offspring of such inter-marriages.
The second migrants to Eritrea were the Hamites (Kushites).

cards.title: 7.2 Size and Population Growth
body: No official population count or census has been undertaken in Eritrea.
According to the information obtained from some government offices and World Population Reference Bureau, the total population size of Eritrea is estimated at 5.1 million.

cards.title: Growth, fertility and dependency
body: No full census has been taken, so figures are estimates. The population grew from about **757,000 (1945)** to **1.5 million (1964)**, **2.8 million (1994)** and about **5.1 million (2009)** – fast growth.
The **total fertility rate** (average children per woman) is about **5**, which is high. At this rate the population was projected to reach about 7.7 million by 2025. About **21%** live in towns.

**Age structure:** about **41.5%** are under 15 and about **6.3%** are over 65, so **47.8%** are dependants. The **dependency ratio** = dependants ÷ working-age people (15–64) × 100 = 47.8 ÷ 52.2 × 100 ≈ **92**: every 100 working-age people support about 92 dependants.
A young, fast-growing population needs more schools, clinics, jobs and food, but it also offers a large future workforce.

lessons.title: Size and Distribution of the Ethnic Groups

cards.title: 7.3 Size and Distribution of the Ethnic Groups
body: Eritrea has **nine ethnic groups**. Without a census the figures are estimates, but they show the main pattern.
**Tigrigna** (about 50%) live mainly in the highlands of Maekel and Debub. **Tigre** (about 31%), the second largest group, live in the Northern Red Sea, Anseba and Gash-Barka.

**Afar** (about 5%) live in the Southern and Northern Red Sea; **Saho** (about 5%) in Debub and the Northern Red Sea; **Bidhaawyeet** (Hedareb, about 2.5%) in Anseba and Gash-Barka; **Bilen** (about 2.1%) in Anseba around Keren.
**Kunama** (about 2%) and **Nara** (about 1.5%) live only in Gash-Barka; the **Rashaida** (under 1%) live in the Northern Red Sea.

cards.title: Where each group lives (summary)
body: **Highlands:** Tigrigna (Maekel, Debub). **North and west:** Tigre (Northern Red Sea, Anseba, Gash-Barka), Bilen (Anseba), Bidhaawyeet (Anseba, Gash-Barka).
**South-west:** Kunama and Nara (Gash-Barka only). **East and coast:** Afar (Red Sea zones), Saho (Debub, Northern Red Sea), Rashaida (Northern Red Sea).

steps.text: **Step 1: Rank by size.** Largest: Tigrigna (50%); second: Tigre (31%).
**Step 2: Regions.** Tigrigna live mainly in Maekel and Debub; Tigre in the Northern Red Sea, Anseba and Gash-Barka.
**Step 3: Only in Gash-Barka.** Look for groups with a single region listed: Kunama and Nara.
**Step 4: Check.** Together Tigrigna and Tigre make up about 81% of the population.

cards.answer: Tigrigna (about 50%, Maekel and Debub) and Tigre (about 31%, Northern Red Sea, Anseba, Gash-Barka); Kunama and Nara live only in Gash-Barka.

cards.title: 7.4 Factors of Population Distribution
body: Other zones, however, support a very low number of people.
In the latter areas, the number of people per square kilometer is very low.
From the highland regions of Eritrea, the number of people living in the Maekel region and the Debub region is high.
In the Maekel region for example, population density is about 125 per square kilometer.
The lowland regions of Eritrea are sparsely populated.

cards.title: Why people cluster
body: Water, milder climate, soil, roads, jobs, history of settlement.

cards.title: Why some areas empty
body: Drought risk, malaria lowlands, few services, pastoral range needs space.

cards.title: Why population is unevenly distributed
body: Population is concentrated in the highlands: about **125 people per km²** in Maekel and **44** in Debub, compared with only about **9–10** in the Northern and Southern Red Sea zones.

**Relief and climate:** highlands attract people with cool temperatures, adequate rain and fertile soils; rugged slopes and rain-shadow areas within them do not. The hot, humid lowlands discourage settlement, except where groundwater and alluvial soils are available.

**Natural resources:** grazing land (southern Gash-Barka – Shambiko, Shilalo, Om Hajer – and the Buri Peninsula), water (riverside and spring settlements such as Shieb and Foro; marsas at river mouths on the coast) and fishing grounds (villages such as Hirgigo, Zula, Thio and Eddi).
**Human factors:** roads, towns, jobs, services and the history of settlement also pull people, which is why Asmara and other highland towns are densely populated.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following countries is the most sparsely populated?
cards.why: Sparsely populated means having few people per square kilometer. Brazil, despite its large population, has a huge land area (including the Amazon rainforest), resulting in a low population density compared to densely populated countries like Bangladesh or Singapore.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following statements is **correct**?

options.A: population distribution is the average number of people per unit square
options.B: population density is the spread of people on the earth’s surface
options.C: harsh climatic and impenetrable vegetation cover areas the world uninhabited
options.E: Africa is the most densely continent

cards.why: Statement C is correct because extreme environmental factors like **harsh climates** (e.g., deserts, polar regions) and **thick vegetation** (e.g., dense rainforests) make areas difficult to settle, leaving them largely uninhabited.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which one of the following is **not** a factor that affects population distribution and density?
cards.why: All the listed options (Climate, availability of grazing land, mineral resources, and soil fertility) are major physical factors that determine where people choose to live and how densely populated an area becomes.

cards.title: Exam question, solved
cards.problem: Which of the following is **not** moderate densely populated area?  A) Tropical savannah  B) Temperate grasslands  C) Temperate coastal land  D) Mediterranean coast land  E) Humid tropics

steps.text: **Step 1.** **Humid tropics** (like the Amazon or Congo basins) are generally **sparsely populated** due to dense rainforests, poor soils (leaching), and high prevalence of tropical diseases.
**Step 2.** They do not fit the 'moderate' density category like grasslands or coastal areas.

tips.text: Eritrea has nine ethnic groups who are unevenly distributed throughout the country. These nine ethnic groups are the descendants of the Semitic, Kushitic and Nilotic families.
The root for all of these families and ethnic groups is, however, the Pygmoid, the earliest inhabitants of Eritrea.
Although no official census has been undertaken in Eritrea, the total population size of the country is estimated at present to be about 5.1 million.
The population is unevenly distributed due to several physical and human factors.
Why people cluster: Water, milder climate, soil, roads, jobs, history of settlement.
Why some areas empty: Drought risk, malaria lowlands, few services, pastoral range needs space.

cards.front: **Tap:** Name two reasons the central highlands are more crowded.
cards.back: Milder temperatures + more reliable (though still modest) rain → farming and towns. Also the main road / rail spine and capital services sit there.
